newsitem.title: CHINA: Beijing official says wants to learn from Washington.
newsitem.headline: Beijing official says wants to learn from Washington.

text.p: A top Beijing official praised Marion Barry, mayor of Washington D.C., on Monday for boosting ties between the two capitals and said he wanted to learn from the U.S. city's urban development.

"Beijing wants to learn from the experiences of urban development of cities in other countries, especially Washington's experiences in this regard," Wei Jianxing, Communist Party chief of Beijing, was quoted by the official Xinhua news agency as saying.
Wei, also a member of the party's powerful Politburo, said he hoped the two cities would boost economic and other exchanges, the agency said.
Washington is virtually bankrupt. The financial management of the District of Columbia was taken over in February 1995 by a Federal control board.
Barry is on a six-day visit to the Chinese capital at the invitation of Beijing's acting mayor Jia Qinglin.
Jia assumed his post last month in a long-delayed reshuffle following a 1995 corruption scandal involving a vice-mayor, who later committed suicide.
Barry, a liberal Democrat and civil rights leader, is no stranger to controversy, having served a jail term in 1990 on a Federal drug charge.
